newsitem.title: USA: AMD says orders improved in Q4.
newsitem.headline: AMD says orders improved in Q4.

text.p: Advanced Micro Devices Inc, a maker of semiconductor chips, on Monday said orders improved significantly in its recently completed fourth quarter.

"Our book-to-bill ratio exceeded 1:1 for the first time since the second quarter of 1995," the company said in a statement along with its fourth quarter earnings. "Customers have worked through excess inventories and order patterns currently reflect normal consumption rates."
A book-to-bill ratio of 1.0 means that for every $1.00 of orders, the company shipped $1.00 of products. A ratio over 1.0 means more orders are being taken than products shipped.
Earlier, AMD reported a net loss of $0.15 a share versus a profit of $0.07 a share one year ago. Analysts had expected the company to lose $0.19 a share, according to First Call.
The company said an increase in sales from the third quarter coupled with cost control measures helped it curb its operating loss.
Fourth quarter sales totaled $496 million, up from $456 million in the fiscal third quarter ended Sept. 29. The company reported sales of $595 million in the fourth quarter one year ago.
AMD also said shipments of its AMD-K5 and AMD-K5-PR133 microprocessors contributed to sales.
